facts.text: Royal Oak is a city in Oakland County on the Woodward Corridor, with Woodward Avenue (M-1) running along its west side, I-75 along its east side and I-696 along its south side.
Royal Oak was named in 1819 by Territorial Governor Lewis Cass, incorporated as a village in 1891 and reincorporated as a city in 1921.
Main, Washington and other downtown Royal Oak streets have pedestrian streetscapes with brick paving, street furniture, and tree and flower plantings.
Centennial Commons, a two-acre downtown park, opened in 2021 to coincide with Royal Oak's 100th anniversary and sits at the heart of a development that includes a new city hall and police station.

Each November, Royal Oak Holidays kicks off with the Lighting of the Park, a ceremony on the steps of the Royal Oak Public Library that culminates in lighting Centennial Commons, including its Giant Oak Tree.
Royal Oak is often called the City of Trees, and in most residential neighborhoods large trees line both sides of the street and meet overhead in a thick canopy.
Much of the Detroit Zoo is in Royal Oak, with portions extending into neighboring Huntington Woods.
The Royal Oak Farmers Market occupies a building at the corner of 11 Mile Road and Troy Street that was erected in 1927.
The National Shrine of the Little Flower Basilica, with its limestone church and tower, is a prominent landmark in the city.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Royal Oak, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation in Royal Oak, MI. Tree wraps, canopy lighting and roofline runs for homes under the city's big trees. Free estimates.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Royal Oak, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Tree wraps, canopy lighting and clean roofline runs for Royal Oak homes, planned around the big trees and removed once the season is over.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: In Royal Oak, the trees often decide the design. Across most neighborhoods, big trees stand on both sides of the street and close into a canopy overhead, so a lit trunk or canopy can do as much for a house as its roofline. We look at what stands in the yard, how branches hang over the eaves and where the house is most visible from the sidewalk, then build the display around it. Trunks get even wraps from the base to the first limbs, higher branches are reached from the bucket truck where the property allows, and the roofline gets a clean run that works around overhanging limbs. Removal after the holidays is built into the plan.
considerations: When limbs hang over the eaves, a roofline run needs planning so the lights sit straight and branches are less likely to rub the strands in the wind. We check clearance during the estimate and adjust the layout where a limb is in the way.

The big trees along Royal Oak streets are not always on the homeowner's side of the sidewalk. We center the design on trees in your yard, and if a tree near the curb is part of your plan, it is worth confirming with the city first.

Royal Oak Holidays begins in November with the Lighting of the Park downtown. A house lit in time for that kickoff needs an early spot on the schedule. Installs commonly start in October, and the first requests of the fall have the most date choices.
faq: Can you light a Royal Oak home with big trees out front?

Yes. Tree-heavy lots like the ones common in Royal Oak are what our bucket-truck crews plan for. Send your address for a free estimate, and we will look at the house, the trees and the power before designing anything.
How high up a tree can you light?

It depends on the tree and the access. Trunks and lower limbs are wrapped from the ground or a ladder, and the bucket truck reaches higher branches where there is room to set up. At the estimate we check height, access and overhead wires and tell you what is practical.
What if my house is mostly hidden by trees?

Then the trees become the display. Wrapped trunks and lit canopies can carry a house that is hard to see from the street, with a simpler roofline run or a lit entry to finish it. We will sketch out the options during the estimate.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Royal Oak, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Commercial holiday lighting in downtown Royal Oak, MI. Storefront outlines, window framing, bistro lights and tree wraps for businesses. Free estimate.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Royal Oak, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Storefront outlines, bistro strands and wrapped trees for Royal Oak businesses, planned for people on foot.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Royal Oak is built for walking. Main and Washington have brick-paved streetscapes lined with street furniture, trees and flower plantings, and Centennial Commons, a two-acre park, anchors the center. When the Lighting of the Park opens Royal Oak Holidays each November, the downtown season is underway. People pass storefronts here on foot, so the details count: an even outline on the facade, windows framed without gaps, string lights across a patio, wrapped trees at the door. We design for that close view, plan work around your hours and sidewalk traffic, keep the display running through the holidays and clear it away when the season closes.
considerations: Downtown sidewalks carry people from morning into the evening, so we plan lift and ladder work to limit disruption, keep cords off walking surfaces and confirm timing with you in advance. Early starts before stores open are one option we can discuss during the walkthrough.

The trees and planters along Main and Washington are part of the city's streetscape. We light what belongs to your property, such as the facade, windows, awnings and patio, and recommend checking with the city or your landlord before anything is attached to street trees or fixtures.

Not every downtown business is at street level. Offices and upstairs tenants can share a building outline with the storefront below, and a property manager can coordinate one plan for the whole facade instead of several tenants each hanging their own.
faq: Do you light storefronts in downtown Royal Oak?

Yes. Shops, restaurants, mixed-use buildings and upstairs offices in Royal Oak can set up a walkthrough and free estimate. Mention your hours and any patio, and the walkthrough will cover design, installation, upkeep through the holidays and removal for the whole frontage.
When should a downtown business book?

Earlier than you might expect. Royal Oak Holidays starts in November, so businesses that want to be lit for the kickoff should plan in late summer or early fall. A later request is still worth making; the walkthrough will show what the remaining schedule allows.
Do you do patio and bistro lighting?

Yes. Bistro string lighting over patios and walkways is one of the services we offer businesses, and it pairs naturally with a lit storefront for the holidays. We plan the spans, attachment points and power during the walkthrough and include them in the estimate.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Royal Oak, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent Christmas lights in Royal Oak, MI. A discreet roofline track with app control, placed to stay visible beneath overhanging limbs. Free estimate.
permanent-lighting.h1: Permanent Lighting in Royal Oak, MI
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: App-controlled roofline lighting that stays up all year, planned around the trees that shade Royal Oak streets.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Under Royal Oak's canopy, a roofline can disappear behind branches for much of the year. Permanent lighting brings it forward. Mounted in a slim track beneath the eaves, the lights answer to an app on your phone, so the outline of the house shows up through the trees on any evening you choose. Warm white carries the holidays, team colors mark a big game, and a gentle accent glow makes the house easy to find after dark in every season. We plan the runs around overhanging limbs and existing trim, keep the power connections tidy and show you the app on install day. Once installed, it stays up, so there is nothing to haul out each November.
considerations: Permanent lights stay on the house through every season, including summer when the leaves are full. We look at how limbs sit near the roofline and place the track where the lights show clearly and are least exposed to rubbing branches. Some homeowners schedule a trim first.

Permanent lighting attaches to the house, so if you rent, live in a condo or follow neighborhood guidelines, confirm approval first. The estimate describes the hardware and placement clearly enough to share with a landlord, an association or anyone else who needs to sign off.

Set the season once. The app lets you schedule colors in advance, so the house can shift to warm white for Christmas, orange for Halloween or red, white and blue for the Fourth of July without anyone touching a switch.
faq: Can I get permanent lighting on a Royal Oak home?

Yes. Permanent roofline lighting is available to Royal Oak homeowners throughout the city. The free estimate looks at your eaves, roofline, power and nearby trees, and the written estimate describes the layout and what is included.
Will the trees block the lights?

Leaves can soften the view in summer, but a roofline is usually still visible from the street and sidewalk, and in winter the branches are bare. We check sight lines during the estimate and place the runs where they show most clearly.
Do I have to take anything down after the holidays?

No. Permanent lighting stays in place all year. After the holidays you switch the app to another scene or an everyday schedule, and the track stays put under the eaves. If you add seasonal tree wraps, those come down after the season.
